newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. to set up second military warehouse in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to set up second military warehouse in Qatar.

text.p: The U.S. military is setting up a second warehouse in the Gulf state of Qatar to preposition heavy arms and equipment which could help counter any possible threat to the oil-rich region, a U.S. diplomat said on Monday.

"Tenders for the construction of this facility (the second) have been issued and the contract will be awarded in mid-June," U.S. deputy chief of mission Todd Schwartz was quoted as telling the local English-language Peninsula newspaper.

"Located 50 km (30 miles) southwest of Doha, the Site Two will house an ammunition storage depot, guard towers, an ammunition inspection facility and related support facilities, besides access roads, fencing and lighting," Schwartz said.
The project is estimated to cost between $50 and $100 million, he said.
Schwartz said Site Two would be bigger than Site One, where work was started last year.
Site One is designed to store tanks, trailers, trucks, air defence armament, artillery and communications for U.S. ground forces.
Schwartz said the equipment and artillery prepositioned in Qatar would be enough to supply a heavy combat brigade of 3,000 to 4,000 troops.

The facilities are part of a defence treaty which Qatar and the United States signed immediately after the 1991 Gulf War in which both countries joined other coalition partners to expel Iraq from Kuwait.
Schwartz said the United States did not intend to station any ground troops in Qatar, but said some caretaker personnel would be posted at the facilities to provide maintenance.
